correctness.summary: Exact algebra gives B=(D+L^T)^{-1}(D-L^T D^{-1}L)(D+L)^{-1}, hence the iff SPD condition ||D^{-1/2}LD^{-1/2}||_2<1. Under that condition, an inverse-dominance identity places the preconditioned spectrum in (0,1], while an exact error identity gives the quadratic weak-coupling norm and condition-number bounds. The first-order uniqueness calculation, the rational SPD/indefinite counterexample, and the exact two-block spectrum were checked algebraically and by compact deterministic numerical verification.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Classical GS/SGS/SSOR, extrapolated GS, additive and multiplicative splitting frameworks, and modern additive smoothers were searched using both terminology and exact algebraic forms. The specific diagonal-corrected inverse together with its exact congruence factorization, iff SPD threshold, SPD-system counterexample, and quadratic weak-coupling bound was not located. No novelty is claimed for generic extrapolation, additive splitting, polynomial preconditioning, or forward/backward symmetrization. Full texts of Evans--Li--Xue (1987), Evans--Li (1988), and Bai (2003) were not inspected end-to-end; Saye (2026) was inspected only at abstract level, leaving residual coverage risk.

value.summary: The result gives a mathematically explicit additive alternative to multiplicative SGS: its two triangular inverse actions are independent on a fixed residual, its diagonal correction uniquely cancels first-order coupling error in a natural affine family, and its exact positivity threshold prevents unsafe use. It also gives quadratic weak-coupling spectral clustering, a sharp failure example, and an exact two-block spectral formula.

limitations: Finite-dimensional real SPD matrices with a fixed SPD block-diagonal split are assumed.
The proposed additive inverse is SPD only when ||D^{-1/2}LD^{-1/2}||_2<1; SPD of A alone is insufficient.
The condition-number estimate is a worst-case weak-coupling bound and is informative in the stated form only for delta<1/2.
No floating-point stability, sparse-triangular-solve scalability, communication-cost, or performance theorem is claimed.
Standard symmetric Gauss-Seidel remains unconditionally SPD for SPD D and is not claimed to be generally inferior.
Estimating the spectral-norm safety certificate may itself be nontrivial.
Full texts of Evans--Li--Xue (1987), Evans--Li (1988), and Bai (2003) were not inspected end-to-end; Saye (2026) was inspected only at abstract level, leaving residual originality risk.
Independent audit has not been performed.
